section_1.title: The Familiar World: Real Analysis
section_1.content: Briefly review the standard Euclidean metric (distance) on real numbers. Visualize a sequence of numbers (e.g., 1/2, 1/4, 1/8...) shrinking toward 0 as the exponent increases.
section_1.example: A rabbit jumping toward a carrot; each jump is half the previous distance. We see the rabbit clearly reaching the carrot at 0.

section_2.title: Introducing the 2-adic Norm
section_2.content: Define the 2-adic valuation |x|_2. Introduce the rule: a number is 'small' if it is divisible by a high power of 2. Contrast this with the Euclidean view.
section_2.example: A digital 'filter' machine: Numbers are processed. 8 is considered 'small' (2^3), while 7 is considered 'large' (not divisible by 2). Visual: A bar chart where powers of 2 have shrinking heights.

section_3.title: Convergence under 2-adic Metric
section_3.content: Explain that in the 2-adic world, a sequence converges if the difference between successive terms is divisible by increasingly higher powers of 2. Show the sum 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ...
section_3.example: A 'Binary Accumulator' device. As we add terms, the bits fill up from right to left. The 'distance' to -1 becomes smaller in 2-adic space, even though the partial sums grow to infinity in Euclidean space.

section_4.title: The Paradox: Infinite Sums
section_4.content: Demonstrate the geometric series 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ... = -1 in the 2-adic metric. Use the formula 1/(1-r) where r=2.
section_4.example: A 'Mirror World' animation: In our standard view, the sum explodes to infinity. Through the 2-adic lens, the sum stabilizes at -1. Show a numerical 'lock' clicking into place at -1.

section_5.title: Summary and Conclusion
section_5.content: Recap that 'convergence' depends entirely on how we define 'distance'. 2-adic metrics are fundamental in number theory.
section_5.example: A split-screen: Left side shows standard calculus (rabbit approaching carrot), right side shows 2-adic space (the binary accumulator clicking to -1). Both are valid mathematical truths.
